criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/status.rs has a fixture test with three jobs: one with its own landing record (its landing stage equals that record's time minus the outcome), one with no landing record (reported as no evidence, or resolved only by its own merge commit or commit time), and one whose neighbouring job's landing record exists and is not used for it.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff: `each_job_takes_its_own_landing_evidence_and_never_a_neighbours` has jobs `own` (record dated by its host commit, 6.0 min), `none` (no evidence, then MergeCommit) and `near` (a record exists for job 20261029-115900-prev and is not used; JobCommit later). It passes (32 landing tests passed). The `own` assertion fails on base code (73 min by created_at). The neighbour part is weak: base code also filtered by job id, so it would pass on base too.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run -- status` (athena status) on this repository's real records. For the five most recent landed jobs the reported landing durations are each within 3 minutes of the time between the job's outcome and its commit on main from `git log`. For job 20261029-130605-mbpm the landing stage is about 3.8 minutes (outcome 20:41:09 to commit 20:44:56 UTC), not hours. The overall median for landing and rebuild is no longer 273.8 minutes. The producer's job report shows this check.
criteria.evidence: The snapshot has no records/ and only two synthetic commits dated 2000-01-01. `athena status` printed 'jobs none yet' and no throughput section, so the real-records check can't be repeated here. This is a result about the snapshot only. Athena's producer-report-gaps note says the producer did not report this criterion, and CHANGELOG.md says the run was not done in the job's working copy and is left to the verifier. No measured evidence exists that mbpm now shows about 3.8 min or that the median moved off 273.8.

criteria.criterion: When no landing evidence is found for a job, the status output says so for that job. No other job's record is used, and the code path is covered by a test.
criteria.evidence: Throughput::text prints 'landing evidence not found for N of M (ids), so their landing stage is left out of the landing median and no other job's record is used'. The window_without_landing field lists the ids. Two tests assert this text: a_landed_job_with_no_evidence_says_so_and_is_left_out_of_the_landing_median and the three-job test. Both pass.

criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy -D warnings passed, cargo test passed (1719 tests).

findings.summary: The requested real-records validation was not done, and nothing shows the 273.8-minute median is fixed
findings.evidence: The request says 'Validate against this repository's real records, not only fixtures', and criterion 2 requires the job report to show the check. The producer report does not include it (Athena's producer-report-gaps note), and the CHANGELOG hands it to the verifier. The snapshot has no records and no real history, so `athena status` shows 'jobs none yet'. The producer's diagnosis (created_at dating) differs from the request's ('matching picks some other record') and was never confirmed on real data.
findings.location: CHANGELOG.md new Fixed entry; producer report

findings.summary: The JobCommit fallback counts a job as having landing evidence when the evidence is just its outcome
findings.evidence: job_commit_times holds the committer time of the job's candidate commit. That commit is made before verification (the verifier works on the candidate commit), so it always predates the outcome, and outcome.max(t) equals the outcome. Such a job is labelled LandingEvidence::JobCommit, counted as having evidence and included in the landing median. That is the outcome-time stand-in the request asked to replace with an explicit 'no evidence'. The fixture hides this by placing the job commit at 12:19, after the verifier ended at 12:17. Simpler and more correct: read 'the landed job's commit time' as the job's commit on main, or drop this fallback and report no evidence.

findings.summary: Files outside the expected deliverables were changed
findings.evidence: The expected deliverables are status.rs and CHANGELOG.md only. The change adds three fields and load_commit_times to Records in store.rs, and log_commit_times and commit_time to athena-git. The accepted reading assumed evidence would be read through the existing history data. The additions are plausibly needed for the approach, but they are outside the stated scope.

findings.summary: The neighbouring-record root cause named in the request is not tested and may remain
findings.evidence: The function still takes the max over every landing record that lists a JobLanding commit for the job. A later landing record that also lists this job's commit, which is the request's 'picks some other record' case, would still win. The fixture's neighbour record is for an unloaded job id, which base code already ignored, so that part of the test passes without the change. Taking the earliest matching host commit, or requiring that the job's commit is the record's head, would be more robust.

findings.summary: Merge-commit matching uses a substring search over whole commit messages instead of the job's trailer or records
findings.evidence: `message.contains(id)` over up to 5000 first-parent commits takes the earliest mention of the job id. The request says the commit 'carries the job id in its records'. Matching the Athena-Job trailer, or the commit that adds records/jobs/<id>/, would avoid false matches such as a commit that cites the job before it lands. The change also runs one `git show` per job with a candidate on every `athena status`.

summary: This candidate fails: the urgent fix hasn't been shown to work on real data. It changes where each landed job's landing stage ends: first the job's own landing record, dated by the main commit it names; then the earliest main commit whose message names the job; then the job's own commit. Jobs with none are listed as 'landing evidence not found for N of M (ids)' and left out of the median. A three-job fixture test covers this, and fmt, clippy and the test suite pass on Athena's recorded runs. However, the request's core demand, validation on this repository's real records showing landing durations within 3 minutes of git log and the 273.8-minute median fixed, was not carried out. The producer report omits it, the CHANGELOG hands it to the verifier, and this snapshot has no records or real history (`athena status` shows 'jobs none yet'), so I could not repeat it. Three more problems: the job-commit fallback uses the pre-verification candidate commit, which is really the outcome time counted as evidence. The neighbouring-record case the request names isn't truly reproduced. And store.rs and athena-git were changed outside the expected deliverables.
